label: Get the Job — Marketing
overview: The Get the Job — Marketing content helps advisors transition from basic tax compliance to high-value consulting. It is primarily strategic and communication in nature — a turnkey system equipped with communication templates, predictive modelling, and legal safeguards. Tools cover the full outreach lifecycle: automated prospect warming via quizzes and video links, portal invitations, staff training programs, crisis communication, and third-party legal agreements. Entry-level and suitable for all advisors.

diagnostic_entry.primary_question: What stage of client outreach or marketing are you working on — generating new leads, inviting clients to the portal, training their staff, managing a crisis, or formalising a third-party relationship?

support_tools.name: 1st Response & Proposal Templates
support_tools.purpose: A structured email and engagement framework based on 'Agile Theory' project management — breaking new advisory engagements into Feasibility, Planning, and Implementation sprints.
support_tools.core_principle: Reduce the financial risk of a large upfront commitment by starting with a bounded $5,000 feasibility stage requiring only 5 hours of the client's time. Establish clear expectations from the first response.
support_tools.when_to_use: When a prospect or existing client enquires about a large project or new advisory engagement. The first response must set the structure before scope discussions begin.
key_benefits: Establishes the advisor as a strategic partner from the first interaction — not just a reactive service provider
Secures initial paid work at low financial risk for the client (feasibility stage only)
Systematically reviews critical business functions (Planning, Data Management, Marketing) before finalising budgets
Sets clear expectations about the client's time commitment (approximately 5 hours) before any fee is agreed
support_tools.advisor_confidence_note: Lead with the feasibility stage in your first response — never present the full project scope upfront. Position the $5,000 feasibility as the sensible starting point that protects both parties before committing to a larger budget.

steps.name: Frame the Agile approach
steps.guidance: Use the 1st Response Email template to explain the Feasibility → Planning → Implementation sprint structure. Set expectations clearly about the initial stage.

steps.name: Confirm client time commitment
steps.guidance: State that the feasibility stage requires approximately 5 hours of the client's time. Make this visible upfront so there are no surprises.

steps.name: Complete the feasibility review
steps.guidance: Systematically review the key business functions (Planning, Data, Marketing, etc.) to assess structural integrity before finalising the full budget.

steps.name: Move to Planning and Implementation
steps.guidance: Once the feasibility stage is paid and complete, move to the next sprint with a clearly agreed scope and fee.

support_tools.name: Marketing Campaigns, Quizzes & Video Hyperlinks
support_tools.purpose: Automated outreach assets — including the 3rd Quarter Campaign, online quizzes (Growth Fundamentals, What's Applicable, HR Maths), and Vimeo video links — that act as 'micro-steps' between an initial approach and a formal meeting.
support_tools.core_principle: Let the tools do the selling. A 3-minute quiz or a short Vimeo link warms a prospect far more effectively than a cold phone call — it highlights their own operational gaps before you ever ask for a meeting.
support_tools.when_to_use: When you want to generate qualified leads, prime existing clients for a quarterly planning discussion, or warm up a new prospect before a sales call. Use before reaching out for a formal meeting.
key_benefits: Automates outreach — the quiz or video does the qualifying work without manual sales effort
Focuses the client's attention on seasonal risks (e.g., the 'perfect storm' of tax and holidays) and upcoming planning needs
Generates warm leads: prospects who engage with the content are far more receptive to a follow-up call
Three quizzes cover different entry points: Growth Fundamentals (general), What's Applicable (module fit), HR Maths (people cost awareness)
support_tools.advisor_confidence_note: Embed the relevant video hyperlink in your email signature, or send a targeted text message with the quiz link. When you follow up, frame the call as reviewing their quiz results — not as a sales call. Monitor completions to prioritise your follow-up sequence.

steps.name: Identify target clients or prospects
steps.guidance: Build a list of clients who need a nudge for quarterly planning, or cold targets who require warming before a formal approach.

steps.name: Embed or send the micro-step asset
steps.guidance: Embed a Video Hyperlink in your email signature, or send a direct text or email with the 3-minute quiz link. Use the Get.TCM.Quiz link email template for the quiz approach.

steps.name: Monitor quiz completions
steps.guidance: Track who has completed the quiz. Favourable completions indicate a warm prospect ready for a follow-up call.

steps.name: Book the meeting
steps.guidance: Contact engaged prospects within 48 hours. Frame the call around their quiz results — you are reviewing their answers, not pitching a service.

support_tools.name: 90-Day Best Practice Training Outreach
support_tools.purpose: A structured 4–5 session Zoom-based training program for a client's administrative staff, teaching correct use of accounting software (Xero), transaction coding, and monthly quality control.
support_tools.core_principle: Proactively solve the 'birds-nest nightmare' at the source — poorly coded accounts cost the advisor time and the client money at year-end. Training the admin team creates a new revenue stream while preventing costly mistakes.
support_tools.when_to_use: When a client uses digital accounting software but has an untrained or inexperienced admin team. Use after the portal is set up and the client relationship is established.
key_benefits: Creates a new recurring revenue stream ($1,500–$1,800 + GST, billed in 3 monthly instalments)
Reduces year-end clean-up time by training staff on correct coding and quality control upfront
Prevents 'surprise' tax bills from the IRD caused by incorrect data entry
Structured training plan covers 4–5 Zoom sessions: software coding, transaction generation, monthly quality control, 90-day close-off
support_tools.advisor_confidence_note: Standardise the fee at $1,500 + GST for local traders and $1,800 + GST for businesses trading internationally. Bill in 3 monthly instalments to reduce friction. Present it as an investment in the client's admin team, not a training product.

support_tools.name: Crisis Management Templates
support_tools.purpose: Email and phone scripts (3 emails, 2 phone scripts) for reaching out to clients during economic lockdowns, supply chain disruptions, or sudden market downturns. Includes tools to model 'Good, Bad & Ugly' cash flow scenarios.
support_tools.core_principle: Demonstrate immense value during a crisis at no initial cost. Helping a client through a crisis cements the relationship far more than any sales pitch — and it naturally leads to paid programming when stability returns.
support_tools.when_to_use: Whenever an active client faces a sudden economic downturn, lockdown, or severe market disruption. Use immediately — do not wait for the client to reach out.
key_benefits: Provides a compassionate, structured outreach framework — not a generic check-in email
Helps clients model three revenue scenarios ('Good, Bad & Ugly') before cash pressure becomes a crisis
Prepares clients to secure bank funding before credit divisions are overwhelmed
Focuses the client on one of three core functions: Getting Organised, Getting the Job, or Doing the Job
support_tools.advisor_confidence_note: Reach out before the client contacts you. Use the email template first, then follow up by phone using the provided scripts. Position the 'Good, Bad & Ugly' scenario modelling as a free tool you are offering during a difficult period — ask for nothing in return at this stage.

support_tools.name: Portal Invitations & System Checklists
support_tools.purpose: Email invitation templates (from direct to conservative) for onboarding clients to the Advisor-e portal, plus internal firm checklists for setting up client accounts via the Xero API.
support_tools.core_principle: Standardise the firm's onboarding process. Set up the client's portal with their data before they ever log in — so their first experience is a fully populated dashboard, not an empty screen.
support_tools.when_to_use: When onboarding a new or existing client to the Advisor-e portal, or when transitioning a client to the firm's advisory software platform. Also used internally by staff managing client setups.
key_benefits: Three email variations (direct to conservative) allow the advisor to match the invitation tone to the client relationship
Framing the portal as a 'mental gym' lowers client intimidation around new technology
Internal checklists ensure consistent setup: Xero API import, financial data load, menu customisation, 15-minute orientation session
Grants the client 24/7 access to a centralised hub for agendas, action plans, and templates
support_tools.advisor_confidence_note: Set up the client's entity and import their financial data before sending the invitation — never invite them to an empty portal. Follow up within 48 hours of sending the email using a phone script to book a 15-minute Zoom orientation. Treat the portal release as a process, not a single email event.

steps.name: Create the client entity via Xero API
steps.guidance: Use the 'Let the Software do the Lifting' checklist. Mass-create business entities, import their cash volatility and financial performance data, and customise the Client Service Plan menus.

steps.name: Select and send the invitation email
steps.guidance: Choose from the three Get.Invitation email variations. Direct tone suits established clients; conservative ('mental gym') tone works better for new or technology-hesitant clients.

steps.name: Follow up within 48 hours
steps.guidance: Call within 48 hours to personally walk them through their first login and book a 15-minute Zoom orientation session.

support_tools.name: Third-Party Collaboration & Legal Templates
support_tools.purpose: Formal templates for formalising relationships with external parties — including the Mutual Confidentiality Agreement (NDA), Banker Login email, and External Advisor Consent form.
support_tools.core_principle: Protect the firm's intellectual property and the client's data while systematically building referral networks with bankers and other external advisors. Every third-party relationship must be formalised before sensitive information is shared.
support_tools.when_to_use: When a client or prospect needs to share sensitive operational data; when revealing proprietary consulting frameworks to map a custom software application; when inviting a banker or external advisor into the client's portal. Also used to build mutual referral relationships.
key_benefits: NDA protects the advisor's intellectual property and the client's confidential financial data during project evaluations
Banker Login email builds referral networks — the banker gains visibility of the client's exposure dashboard and may send unattached clients to the advisor
External Advisor Consent form secures formal privacy compliance before granting third-party portal access
Builds transparency with lenders, potentially accelerating the client's funding process
support_tools.advisor_confidence_note: Introduce the NDA during the Feasibility stage of any new project where proprietary frameworks will be shared. Use the Banker Login email as a deliberate referral strategy — the template includes a script reminding the banker that you accept referrals for advisory work without requiring the client to leave their existing compliance accountant.

support_tools.name: Website Blurbs & Messaging Plan
support_tools.purpose: Ready-to-use website copywriting templates structured around four 'bands' (Attention, Problem, Position, Solution), plus a slide deck for mapping out the firm's global messaging strategy, marketing timeline, and service ascension diagram.
support_tools.core_principle: Answer the client's core question ('How much is enough?') within the first 7–20 seconds of visiting the website. All social media, blog, and website content must align to the target market's specific problems — not the firm's credentials.
support_tools.when_to_use: When revamping the firm's website, aligning the team's marketing messaging, or building a comprehensive communication and seminar timeline. Use the Messaging Plan when the firm needs to identify their core Concept Domains and target market problems.
key_benefits: Pre-written copy for all four homepage bands — eliminates hours of copywriting from scratch
Service descriptions position the firm's offering aspirationally (from Basic Accounting to Legacy Package)
Messaging Plan aligns all marketing channels (social media, blog, seminars) to the same target market problems
Ascension diagram makes the firm's value ladder visible to prospects from the first website visit
support_tools.advisor_confidence_note: Use the four-band structure for the homepage: Band 1 grabs attention, Band 2 names the client's problem, Band 3 positions the firm as the solution, Band 4 shows how to engage. The Messaging Plan slide deck should be completed at the firm level before individual marketing assets are produced.

advisor_guidance.sequence: Follow the 4-step outreach sequence: (1) Internal system preparation — set up client portals before contact. (2) Micro-step outreach — quiz or video link to warm the prospect. (3) Portal invitation and follow-up — invite and orient. (4) Formalise the engagement — use 1st Response, NDA, or consent forms as required.
advisor_guidance.entry_point: If you are uncomfortable with direct selling, start with the micro-steps (quiz links and video hyperlinks). These assets do the qualifying work for you — when you follow up, you are reviewing their quiz results, not making a cold pitch.
advisor_guidance.legal_protection: Never share proprietary frameworks or client financial data with a third party without the NDA or External Advisor Consent form in place. These are not optional — they are your legal protection.
